newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan share gains evaporate, turn down at close.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan share gains evaporate, turn down at close.

text.p: Taiwan's share prices were higher through much of Wednesday's volatile, electronics-driven session but lost steam in last minutes to finish lower as heavy profit-taking eroded the early gains, brokers said.
Infected by Wall Street's bullish mood, electronics shares helped push the benchmark stock index pushed as high as 9,694.28 in early trade, but late profit-taking reversed the trend.
The index finished 169.34 points or 1.77 percent lower at 9,381.06 compared to Tuesday's 9,550.40 close.
Turnover was heavy at T$189 billion but below the recent T$200 billion-plus levels. Tuesday turnover was T$206 billion.
Electronics shares rose steadily through most of the session but retreated at the end as investors took profits, losing 0.93 percent and intensifying the broader selloff, brokers said.
"Profit-taking was the major reason for the loss, and it appears that the electronic sector will remain in consolidation for a while," independent analyst Michael Hung said.
Brokers said there was no especially bad news to point to.
"On the contrary, the news was on the good side, including the Wall Street rally and the ex-bonus issues of several companies," Hung said.

The weighted index showed sign of weakness in late trade despite ex-bonus issues by 15 companies, including Taiwan's No.2 chipmaker United Microelectronics and Nationalist Party-backed China Development, brokers said.
Brokers said the selloff snowballed in the last 10 minutes as investors dumped even those shares of some ex-bonus firms -- including United Micro and China Development.
China Development, which has sound fundamentals and huge earnings in addition to its 10 percent ownership by the ruling Nationalists, lost T$5.5 to T$130 to the surprise of most brokers.
